intro.help: This intro is a short film that moves as you scroll, swipe or hold the pedal, and stops when you stop. Each line stays until it has been read. Space, a click or tap on the picture, or a press of the pedal brings the next line; holding Space, W or the pedal keeps driving after it. Shift and Space goes back, S or the up arrow backs up, and Escape skips the intro. The full script follows as text.

hero.sceneLabel: Sunset drive over a causeway toward a city skyline and an art-deco tower at the end of the avenue, palm trees on both sides
hero.speaker: Jesús
lines: I'm from Tenerife, where even the sun works overtime.
I'm a frontend engineer, and I solve problems for a living,
especially the ones that turn up on a Friday afternoon.
Before code, I did four years in the army as a combat engineer,
on Gran Canaria, which takes some nerve if you're from Tenerife.
I learned to take orders there, and now I give them to AI.

suspects.description: A police line-up of Jesús's four cats in front of a height chart, each behind a numbered plate. Tom and Kira stand the tallest, Odin a little lower, and Dante, the kitten, is the smallest by a head.

tips.text: This film is not suitable for passengers: it won't move on until you scroll or swipe, because you're the one driving.
Hold right-click over the scene, or hold Q, and the radio wheel opens. Let go over a station to tune in.
For the radio, tap its button, or keep a finger still on the picture (not the pedal) until a ring shows, then lift it.
Space brings up the next line, W or the down arrow drives on, S or the up arrow backs up, and Esc skips to the end.
Swipe up to drive on and down to back up. A tap on the picture brings up the next line, and Skip cuts to the end.
He follows F1, so every subtitle has a pit-lane limiter: the car waits until you've read it, however hard you push.
BABYLON's disco comes as standard, but the dial also has CROCKETT's eighties synth and K-CALIMA's classic rock.
MR. WOLF plays hard rock, LEAVE THE GUN brings the funk and LOVE DADDY spins nineties hip-hop beats.
The car never actually moves. The whole city drives past it, and so far nobody has had the heart to tell the car.
The driver's aviators mirror the scene's own sky: the sunset you're watching is in his lenses too.
At night the road reaches the city: every company he has worked for has its own sign, and every sign is a link.
The film grain changes 24 times a second, like a real reel.
Every station keeps its own clock: switch from one to another and you land mid-song.
The cars going your way keep your exact pace, so nobody overtakes you, and you never overtake anyone either.

army.mirror: Spanish Army (Ejército de Tierra), 2018–2021. Combat engineer in the Batallón de Zapadores XVI, in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria.
cards: Sappers go in first, so that everyone else can follow.
No wonder I ended up in the front end.
army.chipName: Service record: Spanish Army, combat engineer, 2018 to 2021

pwc.line: REACT · NEXT.JS · TYPESCRIPT · ZOD · KEYCLOAK · DOCKER
pwc.mirror: PwC España, 2023–2024. Frontend Developer on Bono Cultural 2023 (React, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, TypeScript, Zod, React Hook Form, Material UI) and B Accelerator Tower (Next.js, Keycloak, Veracode, Docker), in a Scrum team working with Git and pull-request reviews.
cards: At PwC I built the forms for the Bono Cultural, field by field.
Zod doesn't take bribes, so no field got through unchecked.
pwc.chipName: pwc.es: PwC España, Frontend Developer, 2023 to 2024

cloud-district.line: NATURGY · PANGEA · TELPARK · NEXT.JS · REACT · STRAPI
cloud-district.mirror: Cloud District, 2024–2025, a consultancy. Frontend Developer on client projects: Naturgy, the energy supplier, on two products with Next.js and React: Omega, its customer area, where customers manage their bills, usage and contracts, and Monitor, its in-house dashboard of processes, logs and events; Pangea, the travel agency (its main website, with Next.js, Atomic Design, Strapi and Storybook); and Telpark (parking reservations).
cards: At Cloud District, clients rotated faster than this board.
The only thing that never rotated was the coffee downstairs.
cloud-district.chipName: clouddistrict.com: Cloud District, Frontend Developer, 2024 to 2025

logixs.mirror: Logixs, 2025–2026. Full Stack Developer on Bytetravel, a TravelTech offering ancillary services for leisure and business travellers (visas, eSIMs, VIP lounges) through travel agencies and airlines, and on the official portal of Retech, a startup acceleration programme.
cards: Then came Logixs, where I went full stack.
So these days I watch my back, too.

stats.description: This is the pause menu. The first tab is his player profile: who he is and how he works, his skills and his records. The map shows where he has worked, on site or from home base, beside his five main missions. Then his achievement tree, unlocked and locked, and the settings: the radio, the controls, the subtitle size and the language.

map.title: TENERIFE, MORE OR LESS
map.label: Map of Tenerife at night, with its towns renamed and Gran Canaria in a box in the corner. Mission 1 is in Gran Canaria's capital, mission 2 at the dock on Tenerife's north-east coast, and missions 3, 4 and 5 at home base, in the caldera.
map.source: Relief and coast: SRTM, GMTED2010 and ETOPO1 (public domain).

player.title: ABOUT ME
player.bio: I sweat the user experience: smooth interfaces, truly responsive, nothing mass-produced. I use AI as a tool, not an autopilot, always inside my own layer of security, restrictions and configuration.
player.alt: Jesús drawn as a game character: gold aviators, a dark hoop earring, a beard and a striped tee, with Dante, a cream lynx-point kitten with blue eyes, on his shoulder as player 2.
